```{r}
#| include: false
library(gt)
library(countdown)

# One table style for every slide table (instructor convention: gt tables).
slide_table <- function(df) {
  gt(df) |>
    fmt_markdown(columns = everything()) |>
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(24),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      table.width = pct(100),
      data_row.padding = px(6)
    ) |>
    opt_row_striping()
}
```

<p class="diagram-caption">No new R today. The review is the work.</p>

- You review **your reviewee**. Someone else is reviewing **you**, right now
- The list is on Canvas
- Everything is in the book: **Peer Review And Revision**

## Why Review?

- A **fresh clone** has only what was pushed. It is the honest test of
  "reproducible"
- Reading someone else's analysis closely is how you see the gaps in
  your own
- Your reviewer **never grades you**. You are graded on the review you
  **give** (60) and how you **respond** (40)

## Weak Comments

```{r}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Weak, ~`What is missing`,
  "This looks wrong.", "Where? What? The author cannot find or check it",
  "Figure 2 is confusing.", "Confusing how? No way forward",
  "Rewrite the cleaning section.", "No reason, no specific change",
  "Great job!", "Nothing to keep or change"
) |>
  slide_table()
```

## A Comment The Author Can Act On {.smaller}

- **Where:** Data and Methods, chunk `clean-depth`
- **What I saw:** `filter(depth_m > 0)` drops rows; the count goes from
  1,204 to 1,150 with no sentence about it
- **Why it matters:** were the 54 rows errors, or real zero-depth samples?
  If real, dropping them raises the mean
- **Suggestion or question:** say how many were dropped and why. If zero
  depth is possible here, keep them

A **place** they can find, an **observation** they can check, a
**reason**, a **way forward**. About the work, not the person.

## Step 1: Can You See It?

Open your reviewee's repository on github.com.

- **404?** You never accepted the invitation:
  [github.com/notifications](https://github.com/notifications)
- Nothing there? They re-send it: **Settings > Collaborators**

## Step 2: Clone Fresh (10 min)

New folder **outside** your project and course folders, e.g.
`Desktop/review`.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**GitHub Desktop**

1. **File > Clone Repository**
2. **GitHub.com** tab, pick theirs
3. **Local path:** the new folder
4. **Clone**, then open it in Positron
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Positron**

1. github.com: **Code**, copy HTTPS
2. **New Folder from Git**
3. Paste, choose the new folder
:::
::::

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 10)
```

## You Can Push To Their Repo. Don't.

- Rendering rewrites `report.html` in your copy
- Desktop and Positron will offer to commit it
- **Do not commit. Do not push.** The Issue is the whole review
- Delete the folder when the Issue is filed

## Step 3: Render, No Edits (20 min)

1. Open the folder. **Restart R**
2. Open `report.qmd`, **Render**. Do not edit any file
3. Fill in **Reproducibility check** in the template

```{r}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~`You see`, ~`Do this`,
  "`there is no package called`", "`install.packages()`, render again, note it",
  "Any other error", "Copy the **exact** message. Read their `report.html`",
  "No data, README says why", "Get the file from the author, put in `data/raw/`"
) |>
  slide_table()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 20)
```

## The Template

Copy it from the book (copy button, top right of the block).

- **Reproducibility check:** cloned, rendered, data, paths, README
- **Checklist spot-check:** present / missing / unclear
- **Three comments:** cleaning, a figure, the interpretation
- **One thing that works well**, **one science question**, **top priority**

Write it in a text file first. GitHub does not save a half-written Issue.

## Break (10 min)

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 10)
```

## Checklist Spot-Check (15 min)

Against the **final report checklist**, mark each line present / missing /
unclear.

It is a **draft**. "Missing" is expected. Honest beats kind: they need to
know before Dec 16, not after.

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 15)
```

## Three Comments (45 min)

- One on a **cleaning decision**
- One on a **figure**
- One on the **interpretation**: does the text claim more than the data
  show?

Each: **Where / What I saw / Why it matters / Suggestion or question**.
I am coming round to read drafts.

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 45)
```

## File It (15 min)

1. Their repo: **Issues > New issue**
2. Title: `Peer review: <your name>`
3. Paste; **Preview**; **Create**
4. Copy the Issue address > Canvas **Peer Review: Giving**

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown(minutes = 15)
```

## Your Own Review

Check **Issues** on **your** repository.

- **Read it.** Do not answer yet: that is Dec 7
- One comment = change it, or decline with a reason
- Commits say `refs #1`; the last says `closes #1`
